subject: Packaging options checklist and timeline — next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging options checklist and timeline — next steps

Hi Tara,

Great to talk yesterday — thanks for the time. Attached is a short checklist and the two packaging options we discussed: Compact (metered + standard features) and Core+ (committed throughput + seat pooling + higher SLA). The attachment is labeled "consolidation-options-v2.pdf".

Quick summary and asks so we can scope the procurement request: 
- Expected steady-state throughput (avg tokens/sec) and peak burst windows?
- Do you need VPC/private deployment or is hosted acceptable for the pilot?
- Are there must-have features (fine-grained RBAC, audit export cadence)?

Suggested next steps:
1) Share the checklist with procurement (I can loop them in once you confirm).
2) 30-min technical demo next week to show seat pooling and burst behavior.
3) If pilot looks good, we propose a 6-month committed capacity with a migration credit and a one-time onboarding credit.

I've penciled in some demo times in the attachment and added a short note on the migration credit mechanics. If you want to loop procurement now, go ahead — otherwise I'll wait for your go-ahead.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments:
- consolidation-options-v2.pdf (3 pages)

From: Tara Singh <tara@olivehealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-02T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options checklist and timeline — next steps

Thanks, Jasmine — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from procurement and engineering: 

- Throughput: our platform needs sustained ~1.2M tokens/day across a few internal services with spikes up to ~3.5M tokens/day during business hours. Does the Core+ committed bucket accommodate burst without throttling?
- Seat pooling: we'd like to confirm whether seats are per-user or per-service. We run ML services rather than end-users.
- Pricing: procurement will want to see a sample amendment with committed discounts and an explanation of how migration credits are applied against the first invoice.

Procurement flagged questions on SLAs and termination windows — I cc'd them to keep the thread together. Can we get a short demo this Thursday (10/07) or Friday? Prefer afternoon PST.

Tara Singh
Director of Integrations | OliveHealth
tara@olivehealth.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options checklist and timeline — internal alignment

Team — forwarding Tara's questions and procurement on the thread. Summary of asks: sustained 1.2M tokens/day, spikes to 3.5M, seat pooling for services, sample amendment + migration credit mechanics, demo this week (PST afternoons).

Proposed play (my recommendation):
- Offer Core+ pilot: 6-month committed bucket sized at 2.5M tokens/day (covers most spikes but leaves headroom via burst).
- Commercial: 10% committed discount on Core+ MSRP + one-time migration credit equal to 20% of first-month committed spend applied to invoice after go-live.
- Operational: include onboarding package (2 CS eng days) and a 30-day rollback window in the amendment. Monica — can you confirm availability for two onboarding days in Oct/Nov if the pilot signs?

Notes on seat pooling: recommend we position seats as "service-bound" (i.e., pool assigned to service IDs) — that fits OliveHealth's architecture and avoids per-user licensing friction.

Ben — can you prepare a short amendment draft (redlines) and a quick pricing table that shows committed vs metered scenarios and how the migration credit flow looks on invoice? Marissa — please prep a 20-min demo focused on seat pooling + burst handling; Tara asked for Thurs or Fri afternoon PST.

If we give a concession beyond 10% (e.g., 15% or extended credit), I'd like a T+ approval — suggest we keep to 10% for pilot.

Thanks,
Jasmine

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@olivehealth.com>, OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-02T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options checklist and timeline — next steps and demo times

Thanks Tara — quick answers and a couple of concrete next steps below.

Answers: 
- Burst handling: Core+ committed buckets are configured with a burst reserve; for your numbers we'd recommend a 2.5M tokens/day commit. That covers typical spikes without falling back to metered throttling; the amendment will include burst thresholds and overage pricing.
- Seat pooling: we can license seats to service IDs (service-bound pools). That is standard for customers with service-to-service integrations.
- Migration credit: applied as a credit on the first invoice following activation; we show the credit as a line item named "Migration Credit - OLV-298". The amendment template includes the credit clause.

Proposed demo slots (30 min, PST):
- Thu 2027-10-07 2:00 PM - 2:30 PM
- Thu 2027-10-07 4:00 PM - 4:30 PM
- Fri 2027-10-08 3:00 PM - 3:30 PM

Please pick a slot and we'll confirm. Attached is the sample amendment and a one-page pricing comparison ("proposed-mop-agreement-OLV-298.docx").

Procurement — if you want a tracked redline, Ben can share a first-pass amendment by EOD Friday; otherwise we can take comments after the demo.

Next steps: 
1) Tara to confirm demo slot.
2) Ben to share amendment draft (internal) and pricing table.
3) Marissa + Monica to run demo and align on onboarding timeline.

Cheers,
